paletteProvenance.ownerDecision: Keep it same colour scheme as rest of the website (owner instruction, after the first Season Programme build). The home page's private palette was removed; public/assets/home.css now declares no colour token and paints no surface with a literal. Identity is carried by the home-scoped type remap (--serif/--sans/--mono plus the four-step ladder) and by home-only structural CSS.
paletteProvenance.sharedSourceOfTruth: public/styles.css (not to be edited by this world)
paletteProvenance.singleColourLiteralInWorldCss: box-shadow: 0 8px 18px -12px rgba(29, 31, 27, 0.5) on .home-update-status — an unlit near-black wash kept because it reads on both presses; it is not a palette token.

display.purpose: Masthead only, one per page: --t-name. Always uppercase Barlow Condensed 700.

headline.purpose: Programme section titles: Overture, The Season's Works, Notices, Box Office.

title.purpose: Running-order work names, uppercase, hairline underline that thickens on hover.

body.purpose: Work Sans text at --t-body, 46-62ch blocks; overture one step larger.

label.purpose: Stamps, fold control, status lines, dates: uppercase Barlow, tracked 0.12-0.16em.

typeBindingDebt.note: The home scope keeps the shared variable names while changing what they carry: --serif is Barlow Condensed and --mono is Work Sans. Names are legacy; the world has a condensed grotesque and a text grotesque, no serif and no mono.

shadows.name: stamp-lift
shadows.purpose: The system's only drop shadow; sits under the issued stamp. Not reused, not dark-mirrored (reads on both presses).

motion.name: curve-programme
motion.purpose: The world's curve: reveal and fold openings.

motion.name: reveal-rise
motion.value: transform: translateY(1.15rem) -> none; 550ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.36, 1); delay calc(var(--i, 0) * 80ms)
motion.purpose: Programme unfolding: dated rows assemble on scroll. Transform-only; gated by html.home-motion; observer rootMargin 0 0 -8%, threshold 0.15; --i capped at 4.

motion.name: fold-open
motion.purpose: At a glance / Full programme fold on entry rows.

motion.name: state-swap
motion.value: 160ms ease-out on color / background-color / border-color / text-decoration-color
motion.purpose: All hover and state changes on controls and links.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables reveal transforms, transitions, smooth scroll, and the stamp rotation
motion.purpose: Content is visible by default; JS never hides information.

themeMirror.note: Both plates live in public/styles.css, which this world reads and never edits: :root (light), :root[data-theme="dark"], and the prefers-color-scheme: dark fallback. home.css contains no colour declaration at all, so switching theme costs the world nothing; world CSS must never branch on theme or write its own dark block.

metaThemeColor.owner: public/assets/site.js THEME_COLORS; home.html ships the light value and no override

themeMirror.selection: olive ground with paper text (both presses)
themeMirror.bandHatch: .band-hatch is painted with color: var(--paper) at opacity 0.5 and strokes with currentColor, so the same declaration hatches cream-on-olive in the light press and near-black-on-sage in the night press.

extensions.adoptionBoundary: Shipped on home only (src/templates/home.html + public/assets/home.css). The home world now claims type and structure only: a body[data-page="home"] block remaps --serif/--sans/--mono to Barlow Condensed and Work Sans and declares the four-step ladder, and the rest is home-only structural CSS. All colour comes from the shared tokens in public/styles.css, which every page already loads, so the other pages (projects, gallery, services, arrangements, accomplishments, admin) share this palette while keeping the legacy Playfair Display / DM Sans / DM Mono binding until adopted. Adopt the world on a new page the same way: remap the type bindings in one scoped block, add the page's structural CSS, and paint with shared tokens.

narrative.overview: The home page is the programme document of one working practice — the printed booklet itself, not a poster about it. Everything on the surface speaks that world's native material: rules and folios, a numbered running order of works, dated notices, a rubber-stamped issue line, a full-bleed box-office band with hatch texture. The paper is the site's own warm cream, the ink is the site's own near-black, and the one accent — box-office olive, pale sage on the night press — carries every mark that matters. Home wears the same palette as every other page on the site; the world answers that borrowing with structure, not colour. The visitor reads identity first (the name set as the season title), then proof of liveness (a real "Programme issued" timestamp fed by the content API), then the running order, then the notices, then the booking window. Nothing is centered-trio hero furniture; nothing is a row of equal cards. Depth is letterpress, never lighting: rules from 1px hairlines to a 4px masthead underline, a double olive border+outline on the issued stamp, a diagonal hatch band, and one small shadow under the stamp. There are no gradients, no glass, no rounded surfaces. Motion is the programme unfolding as you scroll — dated rows rise into place, one named control ("At a glance" / "Full programme") opens or closes the running order — and all content is visible by default without JS or under reduced motion. The system currently ships on the home page only, and what home claims as its own is type and structure: the shared tokens in public/styles.css supply every colour, while the other pages keep the legacy Playfair Display / DM Sans binding until adopted.
keyCharacteristics: Site-wide cream paper, near-black ink, one olive accent at folio scale plus (at most) one full-bleed olive band — the world never repaints them.
Fixed typographic scale ladder — folio, body, entry, name — with all display type set uppercase in condensed Barlow.
Letterpress structure: rules, double borders, hatch texture, one stamp shadow; zero gradients, zero glass, zero rounded surfaces.
Live data as identity furniture: the issued stamp and dated notices render real timestamps; the world never fabricates a date.
Two presses of one ink: every token already has its dark mirror in the shared sheet; switching theme is switching print run, not switching design.

rules.name: The Shared-Palette Rule (owner decision)
rules.body: The home page wears the site's colours and no others. The owner asked it to keep the same colour scheme as the rest of the website, and the build complies literally: home-scoped CSS declares no colour token of its own and paints no surface with a literal — its single literal is the stamp's near-black shadow wash, which reads on both presses. The palette is common ground; the Season Programme's identity is carried entirely by structure, rules, folios, hatch, and the condensed type ladder. A new world surface that wants a colour it doesn't already have gets none: it reaches for --paper, --paper-deep, --surface, --ink, --muted, --olive, --line or --brown.

rules.name: The No-Second-Accent Rule
rules.body: Olive is the only voice of emphasis — no additional accent, no gradient to fake one. At rest it appears only as folio-scale marks; exactly one full-bleed band per page may invert it into a surface. Its rarity is still the point: when the band or an olive mark appears on a new surface, it must mean something (a folio, a live mark, a booking action).

rules.name: The Two Presses Rule
rules.body: Light and dark are one system printed twice, and the shared sheet owns both plates: every token has its mirror set beside it, in the same block. World CSS never branches on theme, never writes its own dark block, and never hardcodes one press — consuming the token is what makes the flip free.

rules.name: The Fixed Ladder Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from the four-step ladder (folio, body, entry, name) before any invented size. One-off variants exist only as documented furniture steps; a new surface reaches for the ladder first.

rules.name: The Set-Caps Rule
rules.body: Programme words in the display face are uppercase and tracked; only the δ glyph and real date strings break caps. Never set body prose in Barlow.

rules.name: The Bleed Rule
rules.body: Full-bleed elements reach the viewport edge only via the −7.5% counter-offset of the column gutter, so the band's content realigns with the page column.

rules.name: The Pressed, Not Lit Rule
rules.body: Convey depth with rules, double borders, hatch texture, and the one stamp lift — never with shadows-as-lighting, gradients, or blur. If a new surface needs to feel raised, give it the stamp's paper (#fffdf8 / #1d1d1c) and a border, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Real Dates Rule
rules.body: The issued stamp, notice dates, and masthead latest-notice line always render live content from the APIs; furniture with no real data stays hidden. The stamp's credibility is the whole world's credibility.

dos: Do adopt the world on a new page by remapping the shared type bindings in one scoped block (as body[data-page="home"] does — --serif, --sans, --mono plus the four-step ladder) and adding that page's structural CSS; the shared chrome and the shared palette then come along for free.

Do paint every world surface with the shared tokens — var(--paper), var(--paper-deep), var(--surface), var(--ink), var(--muted), var(--olive), var(--line), var(--brown) — so the press flips itself; public/styles.css is not this world's to edit or re-mirror.
Do set display type uppercase Barlow Condensed from the fixed ladder; track small settings (0.12–0.2em) and leave large settings near 0.
Do render the issued stamp, notice dates, and nav labels from the live APIs; hide furniture that has no real data.
Do use the stamp lift only on the stamp; use borders, hairlines, and hatch for everything else.
Do keep reveal transforms and 160ms colour state swaps; ship content visible without JS.
donts: Don't mix type bindings inside one page: a surface either speaks the Season Programme ladder (Barlow Condensed + Work Sans) or the legacy Playfair Display / DM Sans / DM Mono furniture — never a Playfair heading or mono label beside this world's condensed caps. The palette is shared ground and settles nothing.

Don't give the home world a private colour or a colour literal on a surface: the shipped stylesheet proves the world needs none, and the owner's decision is binding. The admin/form reds in styles.css (--danger and friends) stay in admin and forms.
Don't add a second accent, a gradient, or a glass/blur surface; this world is paper, ink, rules, and one olive.
Don't invent kickers, eyebrows, boxed glyph icons, or hard offset shadows; the only glyph furniture is text itself (δ, ↗, ↓) set in the system's own faces.
Don't fabricate dates, issue stamps, or programme data — the stamp's credibility is the whole world's credibility.
Don't round world surfaces: 0px corners on new components; the 2px chrome micro-radius is inherited legacy, not invitation.
Don't soften box-office copy below full var(--paper) on the olive band; that was a shipped fix, keep it.
Don't write a theme branch or a dark block in world CSS; the shared sheet already mirrors every token.
Don't animate opacity of informative content; reveal is transform-only.
